content: Hi, how can I support your content project today?
I need help writing a promotional SMS for my bakery's spring sale. I want it to feel warm and inviting.

Absolutely! To create an effective promotional SMS, we'll want to focus on three elements: an engaging opening that sets the seasonal mood, a clear announcement of the spring sale, and a call-to-action that invites customers to visit. Each part helps capture attention, convey the offer, and motivate a response, all while keeping the tone warm as you requested.
Here's what I have so far: "Spring Sale at Lily's Bakery! Fresh pastries and breads, now 20% off. Stop by soon!"

That's a great start! I'd suggest a small adjustment to make it even more inviting and to indicate the freshness of the season. For example, starting with a seasonal greeting and mentioning something special, like a featured pastry, can add warmth and personality. Also, a gentle call-to-action can make customers feel welcome rather than pressured.
Could you rewrite it with those changes?
Certainly! Here's a revised version: "Hello from Lily's Bakery! Celebrate spring with 20% off our fresh strawberry croissants and daily breads. We'd love to see you, stop in and taste the season!"
I really like that. Should I mention how long the sale lasts?

Including the sale duration is helpful, it creates clarity without adding pressure. You can add a phrase like, "This week only" or "through Sunday," so customers know when to visit. For example: "Celebrate spring this week with 20% off..."

Great, I'll use: "Hello from Lily's Bakery! Celebrate spring this week with 20% off our fresh strawberry croissants and daily breads. We'd love to see you, stop in and taste the season!" Thanks for your help!
